new_statements.quote: Kugama has stem-initial prominence. Prosodic prominence implies the presence of one prominent syllable per phonological word. Thus, in Kugama the first syllable of the stem is strong whereas the following syllables of the stem are prosodically weak. I mainly focus on phonological evidence for stem-initial prosodic prominence in Kugama. I have not analyzed differences between prosodically strong and weak positions in terms of intensity and duration. [...] [pp. 20-21:] the linguistic proximity of these three languages needs to be investigated, since Satte and Gengle remain undescribed. In Glottolog 4.7 and Meek (1931) Kugama and Gengle are considered as one language. According to my consultants, Kugama is indeed linguistically closer to Gengle than to Satte.

new_statements.rule_in_words: For Kugama (the only described member of the Gengle-Kugama unit): one prominent syllable per phonological word, located on the stem-initial syllable; prominence is diagnosed distributionally (full consonant, vowel, syllable-type and contour-tone inventories only stem-initially; non-initial stem syllables reduced to CV with mostly short front vowels), not by intensity/duration. The language has three contrastive level tones (H, M, L). No data of any kind exist for Gengle proper, so application to geng1243 rests solely on Glottolog's Gengle = Kugama equation (100% cognacy in Meek's 1931 list), which speakers dispute.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned; only one prominent (stem-initial) syllable per phonological word (stem + enclitics).
new_statements.exceptions: Ideophones, reduplicated forms, borrowings and historically complex stems (e.g. sīzáā 'children', bìmɛ́ɛ̰ 'body') may have heavy non-initial syllables; bound nouns, construct forms, prepositions, pronominals and other functional morphemes are ambiguous as to prominence (pp. 46-47).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word = stem plus following enclitics; prominence is stem-initial (morphologically anchored), described for Kugama lexical stems (nouns and verbs). Statement is for Kugama [kuga1239], not for Gengle-specific data.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: geng1243 Gengle [geg] is a Glottolog BOOKKEEPING (spurious) code: Glottolog merges it into Gengle-Kugama kuga1239 because the only Gengle data (Meek 1931 wordlist) are 100% cognate with Kugama. The quoted prominence statement describes KUGAMA (Wam, ISO kow, kuga1239), already checked in Litvinova 2023 explicitly says Gengle (Wegele) itself 'remain[s] undescribed' and that speakers regard Kugama and Gengle as different languages though linguistically close. Cataloguing geng1243 separately would double-count the kuga1239 entity; no Gengle-specific prosodic statement exists anywhere.
